§9.7 Helicity Spinors

9.7 Helicity Spinors

Summary:

  • Helicity spinors are a way to write polarizations 𝜀𝜇 and momentum 𝑝𝜇 in terms of a more natural way (bispinors)

    • This is more convenient specifically for calculating gluon scattering

  • They are written in the weyl representation where 𝜓𝛼 and 𝜒̃𝛼̇ are left and right handed spinors

  • Notice that spin 1 fields transform in the (12,12) representation of the Lorentz group

    • This entails that we can write them as bispinors instead of 4-vectors

  • Remember the mathematical relations for spinors in the weyl representation:

    • 𝜀𝛼𝛽𝜓𝛼(𝑥)𝜓𝛽(𝑥) and 𝜀𝛼̇𝛽̇𝜓̃𝛼̇𝜓̃𝛽̇ are L.I.

  • Some useful relations with these (and the pauli matrices) are

    𝑔𝜇𝜈𝜎𝜇𝛼𝛼̇𝜎𝜈𝛽𝛽̇=2𝜖𝛼𝛽𝜖𝛼̇𝛽̇𝜖𝛼𝛽𝜖𝛼̇𝛽̇𝜎𝜇𝛽̇𝛽=𝜎̄𝛼̇𝛼𝜇

  • For the inner product, defined as 𝜓𝜒≡𝜀𝛼𝛽𝜓𝛼(𝑥)𝜒𝛽(𝑥)

    • 𝜓𝜒=𝜒𝜓

  • All of these spinors are fields. What happens when we use constant spinors?

Definition 9.7.1 (Helicity Spinor).

  • ℝ or ℂ doublets that transform in the (12,0) or (0,12) representation of the Lorentz Group
  • The inner products for these are
  • ⟨𝜆𝜒⟩=𝜖𝛼𝛽𝜆𝛼𝜒𝛽=𝜆𝛼𝜒𝛼=−𝜆𝛼𝜒𝛼
  • [𝜆𝜒]=𝜖𝛼𝛽𝜆̃𝛼𝜒̃𝛽=𝜆̃𝛼𝜒̃𝛼=−𝜒̃𝛼𝜆̃𝛼

  • These products have some identities due to them commuting:

    ⟨𝜆𝜒⟩=−⟨𝜒𝜆⟩,[𝜆𝜒]=−[𝜒𝜆][𝜆𝜆]=⟨𝜆𝜆⟩=0

9.7.1 Momentum

  • For bispinor representation of momentum, we have:
𝑝𝛼𝛼̇≡𝜎𝛼𝛼̇𝜇𝑝𝜇=(𝑝0−𝑝3−𝑝1+𝑖𝑝2−𝑝1−𝑖𝑝2𝑝0+𝑝3)

  • Relations with these spinors are:

    𝑝𝛼𝛼̇≡𝜎𝜇𝛼𝛼̇𝑝𝜇,𝑝𝛼𝛼̇=𝜎̄𝛼𝛼̇𝜇𝑝𝜇,𝑝𝜇=12𝜎̄𝜇𝛼𝛼̇𝑝𝛼𝛼̇,𝑝𝜇=12𝜎̄𝛼𝛼̇𝜇𝑝𝛼𝛼̇.

  • If 𝑝𝛼𝛼̇ is lightlike (that is, det(𝑝𝛼𝛼̇)=0), we can express it in terms of an outer product

    𝑝𝛼𝛼̇=𝜆𝛼𝜒̃𝛼̇
𝜆𝛼=𝑧𝑝0−𝑝3(𝑝0−𝑝3−𝑝1−𝑖𝑝2),𝜆̃𝛼̇=𝑧1𝑝0−𝑝3(𝑝0−𝑝3,−𝑝1+𝑖𝑝2)
9.7.1.1 Little Group

  • These momenta bispinors are invariant under 𝜆𝛼→𝑧𝜆𝛼 and 𝜆̃𝛼̇→1𝑧𝜆̃𝛼̇

    • This is equivalent to a phase shift 𝑧=𝑒𝑖𝜙 if the momenta are real
9.7.1.2 Connecting Momentum and Helicity Spinors

  • Notice that the dot product

    𝑝·𝑞=14𝑔𝜇𝜈𝜎𝛼𝛼̇𝜇𝜎𝛽𝛽̇𝜈𝜆𝛼𝜆̃𝛼̇𝜒𝛽𝜒̃𝛽̇=12𝜀𝛼𝛽𝜀𝛼̇𝛽̇𝜆𝛼𝜆̃𝛼̇𝜒𝛽𝜒̃𝛽̇=12⟨𝜒𝜆⟩[𝜒𝜆]

  • Therefore, we obtain that ⟨𝜒𝜆⟩ and [𝜒𝜆] are the square roots of inner products up to a phase shift

    ⟨𝜆𝜒⟩=2𝑝·𝑞𝑒𝑖𝜙[𝜒𝜆]=2𝑝·𝑞𝑒−𝑖𝜙

    • This allows us to write

      𝜆𝛼=𝑝⟩,𝜆𝛼=⟨𝑝,𝜆̃𝛼̇=[𝑝,𝜆̃𝛼̇=𝑝]

      As for our momentum,

      𝑝𝛼𝛼=𝑝⟩[𝑝,𝑝𝛼𝛼=𝑝]⟨𝑝

    • The dot products of momenta are

      𝑞·𝑝=𝑞𝜇𝑝𝜇=12𝑞𝛼𝛼̇𝑝𝛼̇𝛼=12tr{𝑞]⟨𝑞𝑝⟩[𝑝}=12⟨𝑞𝑝⟩[𝑞𝑝]

  • Here is another identity that is useful:

∑𝑖𝑝𝑖=0∑𝑗𝜆𝛼𝑗𝜆𝛼𝑗=0∑𝑗=1𝑛𝑗⟩[𝑗=1⟩[1+2⟩[2+…+𝑛⟩[𝑛=0

  • To help us with being terse, we write 𝑖⟩≡𝑝𝑖⟩, etc.

    • Our conservation of momentum

      ∑𝑗⟨𝑖𝑗⟩[𝑗𝑘]=0
    • Since the spinors are two dimensions, we can write them in terms of two other spinors (a linear combination)
    1⟩=⟨13⟩⟨23⟩2⟨.2−⟨12⟩⟨23⟩3⟩

9.7.2 Polarizations

  • All polarizations satisfy the relation that

    𝜀𝜇∗𝜀𝜇=−1,𝑝𝜇𝜀𝜇=0
  • Notice that 𝜀𝜇𝜀𝜇=0

Example 9.7.2.1 (Helicity Polarizations).

  • If the momentum is 𝑝𝜇=(𝐸,0,0,𝐸) then we obtain polarizations

    𝜖+𝜇=12(0,1,𝑖,0),𝜖−𝜇=12(0,1,−𝑖,0)
  • as seen before, they are the helicity polarizations

Definition 9.7.2.2 (Reference Momentum).

  • In order to write the polarizations in terms of the momentum, we need a reference momentum. In the case of gluon scattering which this is a very useful tool for, we take the reference momentum to be the momentum of the other gluons.

  • This is denoted by 𝑟𝜇

  • Writing

    𝑝𝛼𝛼̇=𝑝⟩[𝑝,𝑟𝛼𝛼̇=𝑟⟩[𝑟

  • Thus, the polarizations in the bibspinor format is written as

    [𝜀𝑝−(𝑣)]𝛼𝛼̇=2𝑝⟩[𝑟[𝑝𝑟][𝜀𝑝+(𝑣)]𝛼𝛼̇=2𝑟⟩[𝑝⟨𝑟𝑝⟩
𝜀𝑝−(𝑣)·𝜀𝑝+(𝑣)=12[𝜀𝑝−(𝑣)]𝛼̇𝛼[𝜀𝑝+(𝑣)]𝛼𝛼̇=122[𝑝𝑟]⟨𝑟𝑝⟩tr{𝑟]⟨𝑝𝑟⟩[𝑝}=−1
  • since ⟨𝑝𝑝⟩[𝑝𝑝]=0, we have that 𝜀+𝜀+=𝜀−·𝜀−=0
